Risk Management Program
Executive Summary
3M Decatur, AL

1. Introduction

This Executive Summary briefly reviews the major elements of the Risk Management Plan of the 3M Chemical Operations' Decatur facility in Decatur, Alabama.   The safety and health of the employees and environmental responsibilities to the community are priorities.  As an operating unit of 3M, we share in a tradition of environmental, health and safety responsibility rooted in the company's history.  3M was an early pioneer in pollution prevention, creating its environmental policy in 1975.  

2. Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies

It is our goal to prevent accidental releases of regulated and other materials through the proper design, installation, operation and maintenance of the manufacturing processes and the proper training of all employees.  If, despite our best efforts, such a release should occur, the onsite emergency response personnel are trained to control the effects of the release. We also maintain an excellent working relationship with Decatur Fire & Rescue who can provide additional rapid and effective response. 
 
3. The Stationary Source and The Regulated Substances Handled

3M Decatur manufactures specialty films and chemicals for the use in making a wide variety of products.  Three (3) regulated substances are utilized at the facility in quantities regulated by EPA's Risk Management Program.  The following three (3) regulated substances are used at the 3M Decatur Site:

a)           Vinyl Acetate Monomer is a raw material used in the production of adhesives.
b)           Propylene and Vinylidene Fluoride (VF2) are used as raw materials in the production of synthetic rubber and plastic products that are used in the automobile industry.


3M has discontinued production processes that used Trifluorochloroethylene CTFE).   In the 2025 RMP resubmission, Trifluorochloroethylene (CTFE) has been removed from 3Ms Risk Management Plan.
        
4. 3M Program

to Prevent Accidental Releases 

At 3M, we take great care to prevent accidents, including those not covered under the EPA Risk Management Program.  Programs are in place to address accidental release prevention measures required by EPA, Process Safety Management requirements from OSHA, and all notification requirements of EPA's Emergency Response and Community Right To Know regulations.
Beyond government requirements, we have our own standards for continuously improving safety at the plant.  Following is a brief description of the steps taken to prevent accidental releases:
     
	Storage Volume Reduction:  At 3M, we examine opportunities to reduce the volume of chemicals stored on-site, thereby reducing the potential impact of an accident involving those chemicals. 

	Process Safety Information:  Maintain a record of safety information that helps conduct operations safely. This information describes the chemical hazards, operating parameters and equipment designs associated with appropriate processes. The information is used in process training for employees and is readily accessible to operators involved in the processes. The information is periodically reviewed for any appropriate improvements.

	Process Hazard Analysis:  Comprehensive studies are conducted to ensure that potential hazards associated with certain hazardous processes are identified and controlled effectively.  These studies are undertaken by a team of qualified personnel with expertise in engineering and process operations. These studies are revalidated at regular intervals of no more than five years or whenever significant changes are made in affected operations. Findings from the hazard analysis are tracked so that they can be addressed in a timely manner.

	Operating Procedures:  To conduct manufacturing processes safely, we maintain written operating procedures.  These procedures address various modes of operation such as initial startup, normal operations, temporary operations, emergenc

y shutdown, emergency operations, and normal shutdown.

	Training:  A comprehensive safety training program has been implemented to ensure that employees who are operating hazardous processes understand and are trained in the proper operating procedures and safe handling practices.  Refresher training is provided annually on environmental, health and safety topics.

	Mechanical Integrity:  Preventative Maintenance inspections are conducted and documented on hazardous process equipment to ensure proper operations.  Maintained process equipment includes, among others: pressure vessels, storage tanks, piping systems, relief and vent systems, emergency shutdown systems, controls and instrumentation, and pumps.  Maintenance inspections and operations are conducted by qualified personnel with training in maintenance practices or other specialized subjects as required.  Equipment deficiencies are identified, and repairs are completed in a safe and timely manner. 

	Management of Change:  We have established written procedures to manage changes in process materials, technology, equipment and procedures.  Process operators, maintenance personnel or any other appropriate employees whose job tasks are affected by a modification in process conditions are notified and provided any needed training. 

	Pre-startup Reviews:  These safety reviews for new processes and modifications to established processes are conducted as a regular practice.   These reviews are conducted to confirm that construction, equipment, operating and maintenance procedures are suitable for safe startup prior to placing equipment into operation. 

	Compliance Audits:  Utilizing accepted audit practices; we regularly conduct audits to determine whether the procedures identified above are being properly implemented. If program deficiencies are identified, then corrective action plans are implemented to prioritize the corrections.

	Incident Investigation:  We promptly investigate any incident that has re

sulted in or could reasonably result in a substantial release of a regulated substance.  These investigations are undertaken to identify the root cause of the incident as well as any corrective actions to prevent or minimize a release in the future. 

	Employee Participation:  At 3M, managing process safety and preventing accidents are team efforts. We strongly encourage employees to express their views concerning accident prevention issues and to recommend improvements.  
  
	Contractors:  3M hires contractors to conduct specialized maintenance and construction activities.  Prior to selecting a contractor, we conduct a thorough evaluation of the contractor's safety performance. We have a strict policy of informing contractors of known potential hazards related to our processes and the contractor's work.  Contractors are also informed of our procedures for emergency response should an accidental release of a regulated substance occur.   

5. Five-year Accident History
At 3M, no level of accident is acceptable.  We work continually to reduce the number and severity of accidents at our operations.  Within the past five years there have been no significant releases of regulated substances from our facility.

6. Emergency Response Plan
The first line of defense against accidents at 3M is to take action to prevent them, as described elsewhere in this executive summary.  However, we also work to ensure that we are prepared for any potential accident. We maintain a written emergency response plan and have an on-site emergency response team.  The emergency plan includes arrangements for immediate response from employees, notification of local emergency response agencies and the public, first aid and medical treatment, evacuations, and post-incident decontamination of affected areas.  We conduct regular drills including joint training with Decatur Fire and Rescue and Morgan County Emergency Management Agency (EMA) to ensure the proper execution of the plan.  Further, the e

mergency response equipment is regularly inspected and serviced. The emergency response plan is updated to reflect any pertinent changes in our processes that would require a modified emergency response. 

3M also participates in the Chemical Manufacturers Association's Responsible Care Program.

7. Planned Changes to Improve Safety
At 3M, we strive to continually improve safety.  These efforts include designing safety into the manufacturing operations to regular assessments identifying opportunities for safety improvements.  
The primary focus in our continuous improvement program is an ongoing assessment for the minimization of the inventories of our hazardous substances.
